To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
whole-genome sequencing of carbapenems-resistant Enterobacteriaciae (CRE) clinical isolates from a single institution identified a diverse population of strains carrying multiple resistance vectors.
we sequenced a large number of clinical isolates with resistance to carbopenems and identified multiple resistance genes that were present in distinct transposon and plasmid elements.

whole-genome sequencing allows for rapid and precise identification of resistance genes and their associated mobile elements, which are important for directing resources to prevent spread of these organisms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new approaches to the detection and characterization of antibiotic resistance in bacteria.
the identification of the resistance determinants, their mobilization potential, and the strains carrying them.
the detection of resistance genes in mobile elements and the identification of resistance-carrying strain patterns that further active surveillance efforts for antimicrobial resistance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the study demonstrates the utility of whole-genome sequencing for the surveillance of carbapenamase-producing Enterobacteriacea, and that the study is an excellent model of how to perform this surveillance.
the authors have demonstrated how detection of resistance elements within mobile elements and the resistance-carrying strain further enhances active surveillance efforts for antimicrobial resistance.

we have demonstrated how detection of resistance gene within mobile elements and the resistance carrying strains furthers active hospital surveillance efforts for drug resistant strains and how the use of whole genome sequencing is increasingly available and is a powerful tool to define the local drug resistance landscape.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we demonstrate the utility of genome sequencing to identify and monitor the spread of drug resistance in a health care system.
we demonstrate how detection of the resistance genes within mobile genetic elements and resistance-caring strains furthers active drug resistance surveillance efforts.

whole-genome sequencing of clinical isolates can provide detailed strain information, which, when combined with epidemiological data, can enhance the ability to track and control outbreaks of drug-resistant pathogens.
The main takeaway from our work is that

whole-genome sequencing provides a powerful means of refining the strain and resistance profiles of CREs in hospitals and provides a baseline mobilome for ongoing surveillance of new isolates and their resistance vectors.
genomic analyses of resistance genes and their mobilome can provide a nuanced understanding of the local landscape of antibiotic resistance and the strains that carry them.
whole-genome sequencing provides a powerful tool to refine the detection of resistance genes and their mobilization capacity.
